justification: Adds an outside-in check to the daily production alarm. A red result withholds the healthchecks.io ping and alerts the user, so a false red is noise and a false green hides a dead pipeline. Not Critical: read-only, no DB, no served output. Not Minor: it is the alarm that decides whether anyone hears about a crashed job.

pre_impl.existing_data: none in the DB. Reads Railway's GraphQL project query (cronSchedule, nextCronRunAt, latestDeployment.status) for the production environment, with the account token CI already holds as RAILWAY_TOKEN.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Railway marks a cron job CRASHED when its last run exits non-zero and SUCCESS otherwise, but SUCCESS is also what a fresh deploy shows before its first run. So SUCCESS alone cannot prove a run happened; the overdue check on nextCronRunAt covers the 'never ran' case. A FAILED latest deployment may still leave an older active one running, so the message says 'runs older code or nothing' instead of claiming the job is down.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies from the first freshness-alarm run after merge. Today's state is already red: maintenance-mutation and maintenance-security latest deployments FAILED with no build, so the first run will withhold the ping and the watchdog will alert.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: CRASHED stops counting as red, the overdue check is removed, or an unknown status passes
falsifiable_check.observed_red: YES, forced three times: dropping CRASHED from BAD, disabling the overdue check, and disabling the unknown-status branch each failed one test. Restored green, 5 passed. Run against the real 2026-10-21 snapshot it reports 8 checked, 2 red (the two FAILED maintenance deploys).

functions.name: judge
functions.input: list of service-instance dicts from the Railway API, plus the current UTC time
functions.output: list of plain-English problem lines and the count of scheduled jobs checked
functions.if_none: a missing latestDeployment or status is red; a missing nextCronRunAt on a scheduled job is red; an empty list gives checked=0, which main() treats as a failure

functions.name: fetch
functions.input: RAILWAY_TOKEN account token read from the environment
functions.output: production service instances with name, cronSchedule, nextCronRunAt, latestDeployment
functions.if_none: an API error, network error or missing key makes main() exit 1: unreachable is not clean

values.if_missing: a run more than 2h late is reported as 'scheduler stopped'

break_it.scenario: A job crashes at import on every run, as dcp-extract did
break_it.what_happens: Railway shows CRASHED; this goes red; no ping; the user is alerted the next morning

break_it.scenario: Railway's scheduler stops firing a job while its status still reads SUCCESS
break_it.what_happens: nextCronRunAt stays in the past; red after 2h

break_it.scenario: Railway adds a new status name, or the token or API shape changes
break_it.what_happens: an unknown status, or a fetch error, would otherwise read as clean
break_it.how: unknown status is red; fetch errors and zero jobs found exit 1

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- the first freshness-alarm run after merge will be red on the two FAILED maintenance deploys until they are redeployed; that red is correct.
